Arista Networks, Inc. stock (ISIN US0404131064) is trading higher after investors reacted positively to a record second quarter of 2026 and a raised full-year revenue outlook linked to strong artificial intelligence data center demand, with revenue jumping to USD 3.04 billion, up 37.7 percent year over year as of the Q2 2026 report.
AI demand drives Arista’s latest results
According to MarketBeat, Arista Networks last released its quarterly earnings results for the second quarter of 2026 on August 4, 2026, reporting earnings per share of USD 1.02, which exceeded the consensus estimate of USD 0.89 by USD 0.13 and marked a clear beat versus expectations.
In that same Q2 2026 report, the business generated revenue of USD 3.04 billion, compared to analyst expectations of USD 2.83 billion, meaning Arista Networks outperformed consensus by USD 0.21 billion on the top line while delivering 37.7 percent year-over-year revenue growth, as highlighted by MarketBeat.
Arista Networks also reported a net margin of 38.37 percent and a return on equity of 30.65 percent in Q2 2026, underscoring the company’s ability to convert its rapidly growing AI-related revenue into high profitability compared with many peers in networking and data center equipment, according to MarketBeat.
Raised outlook and annual figures support the stock
Beyond the quarterly beat, Arista Networks has raised its full-year revenue outlook to reflect stronger than previously expected demand from AI data centers, where its switches and network software help connect thousands of accelerators and servers in hyperscale environments, as described by TradingKey on September 17, 2026.
The same TradingKey overview notes that Arista Networks’ latest annual revenue reached USD 9.01 billion, with net profit at USD 3.51 billion, figures that frame how the Q2 2026 quarter fits into a broader multi-billion-dollar revenue base and highlight the scale of profitability the company has already achieved at the annual level.
For investors assessing valuation, a recent analysis from Simply Wall St pointed out that the record revenue quarter of around USD 3 billion and the raised outlook reported in early August help explain why the market is comfortable pricing Arista Networks shares near USD 199.53, suggesting the current share price lines up broadly with discounted cash flow estimates despite the recent AI-driven surge.
Analyst sentiment and guidance frame expectations
Analyst sentiment toward Arista Networks remains very positive, with data from Investing.com showing that 31 analysts currently rate the shares as a Buy, 0 rate them as a Hold and 0 as a Sell, resulting in an overall Strong Buy consensus for the stock as of mid-September 2026.
The same Investing.com overview indicates that the average 12-month price target for Arista Networks stands at USD 241.04, with a high estimate of USD 289.00 and a low estimate of USD 185.00, implying about 22.02 percent upside from the cited underlying price level and quantifying how much further many analysts believe the shares can rise over the coming year.
Within that consensus, Evercore ISI maintains a Buy rating on Arista Networks stock with a price target of USD 250.00 as of September 10, 2026, while Deutsche Bank initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a price target of USD 220.00 on August 31, 2026, according to the detailed rating table on Investing.com, giving investors specific institutional benchmarks to compare with the current trading level.
On the guidance side, Arista Networks has set its Q3 2026 earnings guidance in a range of USD 1.060 to USD 1.080 per share, and research analysts anticipate that the company will post around USD 3.70 in earnings per share for the current fiscal year 2026, according to MarketBeat, which provides a numerical framework for future earnings expectations.
As of the latest completed trading session on September 17, 2026, Arista Networks shares closed at approximately USD 199.53 on the New York Stock Exchange, and intraday trading on that day saw the stock move up by roughly 3.02 percent at one point, with a session high reported at USD 204.91 and a prior close around USD 197.54, according to price and trading data cited by MarketBeat.
Additional consensus data from Yahoo Finance show that analysts expect current-quarter revenue for the period ending September 2026 to average around USD 3.33 billion and next-quarter revenue for December 2026 to average USD 3.59 billion, with estimated sales growth rates of roughly 44.11 percent and 44.14 percent for these respective quarters, indicating that high double-digit revenue expansion is expected to continue through the rest of the year.
In the same consensus table, the average estimate for Arista Networks’ revenue in the full fiscal year 2026 is about USD 12.67 billion, rising further to an estimated USD 16.16 billion for fiscal 2027, while analysts model gross margin and operating performance such that the company’s sales growth for the current year is forecast at around 40.64 percent and at 27.56 percent for the following year, according to Yahoo Finance, reinforcing the narrative of sustained but gradually normalizing expansion.
While the strong Q2 2026 results and raised outlook have underpinned Arista Networks stock recently, some analyses also highlight that expectations have already moved up significantly following the AI-driven revenue surge, meaning that the valuation now embeds a fair amount of optimism about continued demand from hyperscale customers, as Simply Wall St notes in its discounted cash flow commentary.
For investors, the key variables to watch over the coming quarters will therefore be whether Arista Networks can continue to deliver revenue growth near the 40 percent level while sustaining net margins above 38 percent and return on equity around 30 percent, as seen in Q2 2026, and whether the company’s Q3 2026 guidance range of USD 1.060 to USD 1.080 in earnings per share proves conservative or aggressive relative to actual demand and the evolving competitive landscape in AI data center networking.

How To Create Income From Arista Networks Stock
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 6:55 AM PDT 4 min read
Arista Networks (ANET) stock costs 63.2 times earnings, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. You can be paid now to agree to buy the shares at a much lower price. So how much income can you earn this way, and would you be glad to own Arista at that price?
Here is the income you get: about 4.7% a year on the cash you set aside, for agreeing to buy Arista Networks at $120, 40.8% below today's $202.86.
So how do you set up this trade? It is simple: sell a cash-secured put.
Sell one put option on ANET expiring 9/17/2027, with a strike price of $120.
Collect about $540 in premium per contract now (each contract covers 100 shares), at today's bid.
Set aside $12,000 in cash per contract to cover the purchase. The premium is 4.5% of that over 352 days, about 4.7% a year.
If Arista Networks stays above $120 through 9/17/2027, the put expires. You keep the premium and never buy the shares.
If it closes below $120, you buy 100 shares at that price, about $114.60 each after the premium, 44% below today's price. The stock may have fallen further by then.
The cash you set aside can also sit in Treasury bills at about 4.3% a year while it waits. That interest is yours with or without this trade, so it is not counted in the income above.
The Business You Would Own At The Strike
If you end up buying at the strike, you would own a business that is growing fast today. Arista's revenue in fiscal Q2 2026 was just over $3 billion, up 37.7% from a year earlier. That beat the guide management had given for the quarter. Revenue has not fallen in any of Arista's last three fiscal years.
Arista also keeps an unusually large share of each sale as profit. Its operating margin, the share of revenue left after running costs, was 43.1% over the past twelve months. The figure for the S&P 500 is 18.6%. Arista carries no debt. It ended fiscal Q2 2026 with about $13.3 billion in cash and securities.
Arista's shares have not become cheaper, though. The stock trades close to its 52-week high. Its price-to-earnings multiple is high against its own past 10 years. You would own the shares only after a large fall, so what counts is how long Arista's growth can last.
How Long Can Arista's Growth Last?
Management expects fast growth in fiscal 2026. On the fiscal Q2 2026 call, it raised its revenue outlook for fiscal 2026 for a third time, to about $12.6 billion. It would not break the latest $1.1 billion increase down by product line, saying all lines should contribute and the mix depends on what it can ship. For fiscal Q3 2026 alone, management guided to revenue of about $3.3 billion.
Management said the whole industry faces tight supply and rising component costs, and does not expect that to ease until 2028. Arista has responded by committing to buy far more parts. Its multiyear purchase commitments nearly tripled in a year, to about $9.7 billion at the end of fiscal Q2 2026.
Arista's sales also depend on a few very large buyers. Management expects one or maybe two customers to each account for 10% or more of revenue. Its two longest-standing partners are Microsoft and Meta.
The income is worth taking only if you would be glad to own Arista at the strike. For that, Arista needs its revenue to keep pace with its 2026 outlook even while supply stays tight. You will see the first sign of that when Arista reports fiscal Q3 2026 revenue against management's guide of about $3.3 billion.

•Delivered 40% growth in non-GAAP EPS year-over-year as the company achieved its first $3+ billion revenue quarter.
•Recognized on the 2026 Fortune 500 list of the largest United States corporations by revenue and named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise Wired and Wireless LAN.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. - August 4, 2026 -- Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large AI, data center, campus, and routing environments, today announced financial results for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
“As we deliver our first $3 billion quarter in Q2 2026, it is clear that our Arista 2.0 platform strategy is compelling,” stated Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks. “Customers see networking as the central nervous system for infrastructure from the client to campus to data and AI centers.”
•Revenue of $3.036 billion, an increase of 12.1% compared to the first quarter of 2026, and an increase of 37.7% from the second quarter of 2025.
•GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 45.4% and 49.9%, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 44.7% and 48.8% in the second quarter of 2025.
•GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.95 and $1.02, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.70 and $0.73 in the second quarter of 2025.
A reconciliation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release.
Commenting on the company's financial results, Chantelle Breithaupt, Arista’s CFO, said, “Our second quarter 2026 reflects strong, broad-based growth, with revenue up 37.7% and EPS up 39.7%. This performance underscores the strength of our market position and the continued dedication of our global team."
•Defending the Keys to the Kingdom: Resilient Infrastructure vs. AI-Capable Adversaries – Join Arista, Anthropic and Palo Alto Networks for a webinar to discuss the future of security in an AI world. Register here: https://events.arista.com/webinar-defending-the-keys-to-the-kingdom.
•Arista Networks was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise Wired and Wireless LAN – The recognition reflects Arista's continued momentum in the enterprise campus, built on its unified, single-EOS architecture spanning the data center to the campus edge.
•Arista introduced the 7060XE7 Series, a next-generation 1.6-terabit portfolio for AI fabrics – The new Etherlink™ platforms deliver up to 100 Tbps of system bandwidth and support Linear Pluggable Optics, cutting interconnect power consumption by approximately 60% compared to traditional pluggable optics.
•Arista detailed new innovations for scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across AI fabrics – The company outlined techniques including multi-planar leaf-spine designs, the open Multipath Reliable Connection
(MRC) protocol, and segment routing over IPv6 (SRv6), aimed at maximizing AI cluster utilization and resilience.
For the third quarter of 2026, we expect:
•Non-GAAP operating margin of 48 - 49%; and
•Non-GAAP diluted net income per share between $1.06 and $1.08.

A reconciliation of non-GAAP guidance measures to corresponding GAAP measures is not available on a forward-looking basis without unreasonable effort because these exclusions can be uncertain or difficult to predict, including stock-based compensation expense and tax benefits on stock-based awards, which is impacted by the timing of employee stock transactions, and the future fair market value of the company’s common stock. The actual amount of these exclusions will have a significant impact on the company's GAAP gross margin, operating margin, and net income per share.

Arista's executives will discuss the second quarter 2026 financial results on a conference call today at 1:30 PM Pacific Time. To listen to the call via telephone, dial (888) 330-2502 in the United States or +1 (240) 789-2713 from international locations. The Conference ID is 5655862.
The financial results conference call will also be available via live webcast on Arista's investor relations website at https://investors.arista.com/. Shortly after the conference call concludes, a replay of the audio webcast will be available on Arista’s investor relations website.

Can Keysight's Advanced Testing Generator Boost Its Growth Prospects?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:40 AM PDT 3 min read
Keysight Technologies, Inc. KEYS has introduced a new 20 GHz PSG XG7-class analog signal generator designed to improve measurement accuracy and increase testing capacity without requiring additional rack space. The instrument combines two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis for engineers working on advanced wireless, aerospace and defense, and high-speed digital applications.
Keysight's PSG XG7-class helps engineers achieve clearer measurements by reducing signal-source noise, offering low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise and a low broadband noise floor. Its dual-channel configuration enables more testing within the same rack space, while output power of up to +22 dBm helps maintain the required signal level, even with lossy cables and test fixtures.
The company's new generator provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset. Its broadband noise floor reaches -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. A hybrid architecture with software-based mode switching further enables the instrument to optimize performance for different testing requirements.
The platform also supports faster upgrades with Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments compatibility, familiar connections and settings similar to previous-generation equipment, allowing teams to reuse existing test procedures. The launch expands Keysight's test and measurement portfolio and helps engineers improve testing efficiency and advance device development.
How Are Competitors Advancing in the Testing Domain?
Keysight faces competition from Viavi Solutions Inc. VIAV and Vistance Networks, Inc. VISN. Viavi is expanding its testing portfolio for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, 6G and Wi-Fi 7/8. The company introduced an Ultra Ethernet Transport validation solution to test high-speed AI data center networks. Viavi has launched the CyberFlood CF50 for application, security and AI workload testing at speeds of up to 100G.
Vistance continues to focus on testing and validation for advanced broadband network technologies. Its Aurora Networks business provides services for integration, user experience and performance testing of network solutions. Vistance has expanded its DOCSIS and PON offerings, including DOCSIS 4.0 and 50G PON technologies, to support network testing, validation and modernization for broadband operators.
KEYS' Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Keysight's shares have rallied 108.3% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 96.0%.
Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 26.05 forward earnings, lower than 28.03 for the industry.
Earnings estimates for 2026 have risen 12.6% to $11.45 per share over the past 60 days, while those for 2027 have increased 18.1% to $14.07.
Keysight stock currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Keysight Introduces Dual Channel Analog Signal Generator for Advanced Device Testing
Keysight's new dual channel analog signal generator increases test capacity without requiring additional rack space.
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 8:00 AM PDT 3 min read
Improves measurement visibility and expands test capacity without requiring additional rack space
SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 29, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) today announced the new 20 gigahertz (GHz) PSG XG7-class analog signal generator, combining two fully independent channels in a single chassis measuring two rack units (2U). Its exceptional low noise and calibrated output power help engineers evaluate device performance more clearly, while the compact dual-channel design increases test capacity without requiring additional rack space.
Across demanding test environments, such as in aerospace and defense, advanced wireless, and high-speed digital applications, noise from the signal source can mask the behavior engineers need to measure. Engineering teams must also increase test capacity while managing limited rack space and avoiding costly changes to established test systems. The new PSG addresses these requirements with low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise, a low broadband noise floor, calibrated output power and two independent channels in a compact chassis.
Key benefits of the new XG7-class include:
Enhanced measurement visibility: Ultra-low noise helps engineers evaluate device performance without the signal source masking critical behavior.
Expanded test capacity: Two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis enable teams to run more tests without increasing rack space.
Improved performance in lossy test setups: Clean, calibrated output power up to +22 decibel-milliwatt (dBm) helps maintain the required signal level at the device under test, including through lossy cables and test fixtures.
Faster technology refresh: Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments (SCPI) compatibility, familiar rear-panel connections and settings aligned with previous-generation instruments help teams reuse existing automation and test procedures.
The PSG provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz, measured at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset, together with a broadband noise floor of -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. Its hybrid architecture uses software mode switching to optimize performance across different applications, while calibrated output power up to +22 dBm helps compensate for losses in cables and test fixtures.
Jun Chie, Vice President, Keysight Core Product Management, said: "For decades, engineers have relied on Keysight's PSG signal generators for trusted performance in the most demanding measurement environments. This new analog signal generator builds on that legacy with the purity, power, and productivity customers need to reveal true device performance and modernize test environments with confidence."

As Yahoo Finance points out, Keysight still faces policy exposure, supply constraints and a lower recurring-revenue mix, which together keep the investment case from being entirely one-sided even with accelerating orders and revenue.
Execution risk is also evident in order timing and supply chain management. According to Zacks on September 16, 2026, the next-quarter earnings estimate for Keysight has risen 27.7 percent over the past month, while management aims to realize 80 to 90 percent of a USD 100 million cost-synergy target on a run-rate basis exiting fiscal 2026, but valuation and timing risks related to policy and supply remain part of the picture.
This mix of strong earnings revision momentum and ongoing execution and policy risk means that, while Keysight’s near-term outlook is supported by rapidly growing orders and an expanding backlog, investors still need to weigh potential volatility around supply, customer mix and macro policy developments when assessing the Keysight Technologies stock.

Keysight helps move innovative OTA measurement techniques toward practical application for emerging 6G devices and systems
SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) today announced a new collaboration supporting research at the Berkeley Wireless Research Center (BWRC) that aims to accelerate and improve testing of next-generation wireless devices. Led by Professor Aditya Muppala at the University of California, Berkeley, the research explores a new approach to over-the-air (OTA) testing designed to help engineers better evaluate the performance of increasingly complex 6G devices and systems.
The wireless industry is exploring upper-midband spectrum, often referred to as FR3, as part of the path toward 6G. As devices employ increasingly complex antenna and beamforming architectures, engineers need faster and more flexible ways to characterize how systems transmit and receive energy across three-dimensional space. These challenges are also relevant to advanced radar and non-terrestrial network (NTN) applications.
Professor Muppala's research will explore new ways to measure radiated performance that could reduce the time and complexity involved in testing advanced wireless systems. By enabling faster, highly accurate measurements and greater flexibility across different frequency bands, the approach has the potential to help engineers evaluate next-generation devices more efficiently, accelerating their path from research to real-world deployment.
Aditya Muppala, Assistant Professor at the University of California, Berkeley, said: "I'm excited to have Keysight behind this research as we explore new approaches to over-the-air antenna measurement. We believe these techniques have the potential to be a game changer for how OTA systems are deployed in real-world environments, making advanced measurements faster, more flexible, and more practical for emerging wireless systems."
Giampaolo Tardioli, Vice President and General Manager at Keysight, said: "Keysight is excited to work with BWRC to advance innovative approaches to wireless testing. By bringing together BWRC's pioneering research with Keysight's test expertise and real-world OTA chamber capabilities, we believe this work can lead to important breakthroughs and help accelerate industry adoption of faster, more flexible measurement techniques for 6G."

Can Keysight's Advanced Testing Generator Boost Its Growth Prospects?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:40 AM PDT 3 min read
Keysight Technologies, Inc. KEYS has introduced a new 20 GHz PSG XG7-class analog signal generator designed to improve measurement accuracy and increase testing capacity without requiring additional rack space. The instrument combines two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis for engineers working on advanced wireless, aerospace and defense, and high-speed digital applications.
Keysight's PSG XG7-class helps engineers achieve clearer measurements by reducing signal-source noise, offering low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise and a low broadband noise floor. Its dual-channel configuration enables more testing within the same rack space, while output power of up to +22 dBm helps maintain the required signal level, even with lossy cables and test fixtures.
The company's new generator provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset. Its broadband noise floor reaches -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. A hybrid architecture with software-based mode switching further enables the instrument to optimize performance for different testing requirements.
The platform also supports faster upgrades with Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments compatibility, familiar connections and settings similar to previous-generation equipment, allowing teams to reuse existing test procedures. The launch expands Keysight's test and measurement portfolio and helps engineers improve testing efficiency and advance device development.
How Are Competitors Advancing in the Testing Domain?
Keysight faces competition from Viavi Solutions Inc. VIAV and Vistance Networks, Inc. VISN. Viavi is expanding its testing portfolio for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, 6G and Wi-Fi 7/8. The company introduced an Ultra Ethernet Transport validation solution to test high-speed AI data center networks. Viavi has launched the CyberFlood CF50 for application, security and AI workload testing at speeds of up to 100G.
Vistance continues to focus on testing and validation for advanced broadband network technologies. Its Aurora Networks business provides services for integration, user experience and performance testing of network solutions. Vistance has expanded its DOCSIS and PON offerings, including DOCSIS 4.0 and 50G PON technologies, to support network testing, validation and modernization for broadband operators.

Keysight's shares have rallied 108.3% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 96.0%.
Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 26.05 forward earnings, lower than 28.03 for the industry.
Earnings estimates for 2026 have risen 12.6% to $11.45 per share over the past 60 days, while those for 2027 have increased 18.1% to $14.07.

Keysight Technologies, Inc. Introduces New 20 Gigahertz PSG Xg7-Class Analog Signal Generator
KEYSIGHT TECHNOLOGIES, INC.
Keysight Technologies, Inc. announced the new 20 gigahertz (GHz) PSG XG7-class analog signal generator, combining two fully independent channels in a single chassis measuring two rack units (2U). Its exceptional low noise and calibrated output power help engineers evaluate device performance more clearly, while the compact dual-channel design increases test capacity without requiring additional rack space. Keysight?s new dual channel analog signal generator increases test capacity without requiring additional rack space.
Across demanding test environments, such as in aerospace and defense, advanced wireless, and high-speed digital applications, noise from the signal source can mask the behavior engineers need to measure. Engineering teams must also increase test capacity while managing limited rack space and avoiding costly changes to established test systems. The new PSG addresses these requirements with low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise, a low broadband noise floor, calibrated output power and two independent channels in a compact chassis. Key benefits of the new XG7-class include: Enhanced measurement visibility: Ultra-low noise helps engineers evaluate device performance without the signal source masking critical behavior.
Expanded test capacity: Two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis enable teams to run more tests without increasing rack space. Improved performance in lossy test setups: Clean, calibrated output power up to +22 decibel-milliwatt (dBm) helps maintain the required signal level at the device under test, including through lossy cables and test fixtures. Faster technology refresh: Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments (SCPI) compatibility, familiar rear-panel connections and settings aligned with previous-generation instruments help teams reuse existing automation and test procedures.
The PSG provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz, measured at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset, together with a broadband noise floor of -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. Its hybrid architecture uses software mode switching to optimize performance across different applications, while calibrated output power up to +22 dBm helps compensate for losses in cables and test fixtures.

Tue, September 29, 2026 at 8:00 AM PDT 3 min read
Improves measurement visibility and expands test capacity without requiring additional rack space
SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 29, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) today announced the new 20 gigahertz (GHz) PSG XG7-class analog signal generator, combining two fully independent channels in a single chassis measuring two rack units (2U). Its exceptional low noise and calibrated output power help engineers evaluate device performance more clearly, while the compact dual-channel design increases test capacity without requiring additional rack space.
Across demanding test environments, such as in aerospace and defense, advanced wireless, and high-speed digital applications, noise from the signal source can mask the behavior engineers need to measure. Engineering teams must also increase test capacity while managing limited rack space and avoiding costly changes to established test systems. The new PSG addresses these requirements with low phase noise, low amplitude modulation noise, a low broadband noise floor, calibrated output power and two independent channels in a compact chassis.
Key benefits of the new XG7-class include:
Enhanced measurement visibility: Ultra-low noise helps engineers evaluate device performance without the signal source masking critical behavior.
Expanded test capacity: Two fully independent channels in a compact 2U chassis enable teams to run more tests without increasing rack space.
Improved performance in lossy test setups: Clean, calibrated output power up to +22 decibel-milliwatt (dBm) helps maintain the required signal level at the device under test, including through lossy cables and test fixtures.
Faster technology refresh: Standard Commands for Programmable Instruments (SCPI) compatibility, familiar rear-panel connections and settings aligned with previous-generation instruments help teams reuse existing automation and test procedures.
The PSG provides phase noise of -135 dBc/Hz and amplitude modulation noise of -150 dBc/Hz, measured at 10 GHz with a 10 kHz offset, together with a broadband noise floor of -166 dBc/Hz at 10 GHz. Its hybrid architecture uses software mode switching to optimize performance across different applications, while calibrated output power up to +22 dBm helps compensate for losses in cables and test fixtures.
Jun Chie, Vice President, Keysight Core Product Management, said: "For decades, engineers have relied on Keysight's PSG signal generators for trusted performance in the most demanding measurement environments. This new analog signal generator builds on that legacy with the purity, power, and productivity customers need to reveal true device performance and modernize test environments with confidence."

Keysight Technologies, Inc. stock (ISIN US49338L1035) is trading firmly supported by a recent earnings beat, after the company reported adjusted earnings per share of USD 3.07 for its fiscal Q3 2026 versus Wall Street expectations of USD 2.46 and revenue of USD 1.9 billion, as highlighted on September 16, 2026.
Q3 2026 results and Q4 guidance in focus
According to Barchart on September 16, 2026, Keysight reported fiscal Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of USD 3.07, clearly above the USD 2.46 consensus estimate, and revenue of USD 1.9 billion for the quarter.
As Barchart reports, the company guided for fiscal Q4 2026 adjusted EPS between USD 3.34 and USD 3.40 and revenue in a range of USD 1.9 billion to USD 2.0 billion, signaling continued earnings growth compared with the Q3 2026 EPS level of USD 3.07 and similar revenue magnitude.
Order momentum and backlog support the investment case
Keysight’s recent performance is closely tied to strong demand from artificial intelligence and high-performance computing customers. As Yahoo Finance reported on September 16, 2026, Keysight recorded a 56 percent jump in orders in its latest reported quarter and finished the period with a record backlog, providing visibility for scheduled shipments into fiscal Q4 2026.
Management’s Q4 2026 revenue guidance of USD 1.930 billion to USD 1.950 billion cited by Yahoo Finance indicates that, at the midpoint, revenue would modestly exceed the Q3 2026 level of USD 1.9 billion and align with the broader Q4 range reported by Barchart, underscoring stable top-line expectations into the fiscal year end.
Order strength and backlog are particularly relevant for investors because they help support Keysight’s ability to convert demand into revenue and earnings over the coming quarters. The combination of a 56 percent order increase and record backlog, together with Q4 2026 guidance slightly above the Q3 revenue baseline, suggests that the company’s exposure to AI-related test and measurement equipment is now a central driver of its near-term financial trajectory.
Analyst sentiment and valuation backdrop
Beyond reported figures, analyst sentiment on Keysight Technologies stock remains constructive. As Barchart notes in its September 16, 2026 overview, the stock carries a consensus Strong Buy rating from 12 Wall Street analysts, with a mean price target of USD 418.42 that implies around 33.5 percent potential upside from the then-current share price level.
According to Yahoo Finance on September 16, 2026, Keysight shares had fallen 11.1 percent over the prior three months despite an 82.1 percent gain over the past year, and the stock currently holds a Zacks Rank 1, which Zacks characterizes as Strong Buy.
The juxtaposition of a double-digit three-month decline with an 82.1 percent twelve-month gain, alongside a Strong Buy consensus and a price target more than one-third above the prevailing price, illustrates a setup in which recent volatility coexists with positive earnings revisions and supportive long-term demand trends. For investors, this contrast between short-term price weakness and strong fundamental and analyst signals is an important part of the Keysight Technologies stock story.
Despite strong demand and a supportive rating backdrop, several risks remain visible. As Yahoo Finance points out, Keysight still faces policy exposure, supply constraints and a lower recurring-revenue mix, which together keep the investment case from being entirely one-sided even with accelerating orders and revenue.
Execution risk is also evident in order timing and supply chain management. According to Zacks on September 16, 2026, the next-quarter earnings estimate for Keysight has risen 27.7 percent over the past month, while management aims to realize 80 to 90 percent of a USD 100 million cost-synergy target on a run-rate basis exiting fiscal 2026, but valuation and timing risks related to policy and supply remain part of the picture.
This mix of strong earnings revision momentum and ongoing execution and policy risk means that, while Keysight’s near-term outlook is supported by rapidly growing orders and an expanding backlog, investors still need to weigh potential volatility around supply, customer mix and macro policy developments when assessing the Keysight Technologies stock.
Keysight Technologies stock price context
Keysight Technologies stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker KEYS and trades in USD; recent price data around mid-September 2026 show the shares moving in response to the Q3 2026 earnings release on August 18, 2026, when, as Barchart reports, the stock fell 5.6 percent on the day despite beating earnings expectations.
For investors following Keysight Technologies stock into the coming quarters, the key numerical checkpoints are the Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of USD 3.07 versus USD 2.46 consensus, Q3 revenue of USD 1.9 billion, Q4 2026 guidance for EPS between USD 3.34 and USD 3.40 and revenue of USD 1.9 to USD 2.0 billion, the 56 percent order growth and record backlog, and the analyst consensus Strong Buy rating with a mean price target of USD 418.42, all as of mid-September 2026.

Keysight Enables UC Berkeley Research to Advance 6G Over-the-Air Testing
Keysight helps move innovative OTA measurement techniques toward practical application for emerging 6G devices and systems
SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) today announced a new collaboration supporting research at the Berkeley Wireless Research Center (BWRC) that aims to accelerate and improve testing of next-generation wireless devices. Led by Professor Aditya Muppala at the University of California, Berkeley, the research explores a new approach to over-the-air (OTA) testing designed to help engineers better evaluate the performance of increasingly complex 6G devices and systems.
The wireless industry is exploring upper-midband spectrum, often referred to as FR3, as part of the path toward 6G. As devices employ increasingly complex antenna and beamforming architectures, engineers need faster and more flexible ways to characterize how systems transmit and receive energy across three-dimensional space. These challenges are also relevant to advanced radar and non-terrestrial network (NTN) applications.
Professor Muppala's research will explore new ways to measure radiated performance that could reduce the time and complexity involved in testing advanced wireless systems. By enabling faster, highly accurate measurements and greater flexibility across different frequency bands, the approach has the potential to help engineers evaluate next-generation devices more efficiently, accelerating their path from research to real-world deployment.
Aditya Muppala, Assistant Professor at the University of California, Berkeley, said: "I'm excited to have Keysight behind this research as we explore new approaches to over-the-air antenna measurement. We believe these techniques have the potential to be a game changer for how OTA systems are deployed in real-world environments, making advanced measurements faster, more flexible, and more practical for emerging wireless systems."
Giampaolo Tardioli, Vice President and General Manager at Keysight, said: "Keysight is excited to work with BWRC to advance innovative approaches to wireless testing. By bringing together BWRC's pioneering research with Keysight's test expertise and real-world OTA chamber capabilities, we believe this work can lead to important breakthroughs and help accelerate industry adoption of faster, more flexible measurement techniques for 6G."
Keysight (NYSE: KEYS) serves technology innovators as a mission-critical design enablement partner for the world's most complex engineering challenges. By connecting market-leading design, emulation, and test solutions across the full life cycle, Keysight helps engineering teams accelerate innovation, reduce risk, and bring new technologies to market faster. Customers across AI infrastructure, communications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductor, and general electronics rely on Keysight to bridge virtual design and physical reality, enabling confident decisions earlier. Keysight's CSG Gains Momentum: Can AI Infrastructure Drive Growth?
Keysight Technologies, Inc. KEYS is benefiting from strong momentum in its Communications Solutions Group (CSG). In the third quarter, CSG generated $1.35 billion in third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues, up 43% year over year, accounting for roughly 73% of total company revenue. The segment also delivered a 70.8% gross margin and 34.0% operating margin.
The Commercial Communications business was the biggest contributor to CSG's growth. Revenues reached $1.006 billion, up 56% year over year, marking its first billion-dollar quarter. Wireline revenues more than doubled year over year and exceeded Wireless revenues for the first time. The trend reflects increasing testing requirements in high-speed connectivity and AI data-center infrastructure.
In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, wireless orders grew again as customers increased spending on next-generation connectivity and the supply chain supporting AI infrastructure. The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) timeline now targets the first 6G standard for March 2029, and management said customers are moving from exploratory research into funded development programs. This can lead to strong growth prospects in the long run.
Aerospace, Defense and Government also contributed to CSG's performance. Revenues in this business increased 14% year over year to $339 million. Orders grew double-digit. Demand was driven by advanced radar architectures, autonomous platforms, satellite systems and resilient positioning, navigation and timing solutions. Backed by favorable trends, KEYS expects fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues of $1.93-$1.95 billion, implying approximately 37% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
How Are Competitors Faring?
Viavi Solutions Inc. VIAV is a leading provider of network test, monitoring and service enablement solutions to diverse sectors across the globe. The product portfolio of the company offers end-to-end network visibility and analytics that help build, test, certify, maintain, and optimize complex physical and virtual networks. Revenue growth in NSE remains tied to demand from the data center ecosystem and aerospace and defense markets. NSE revenues rose 69.2% year over year to $353.9 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.
Teradyne, Inc. TER develops automated test equipment and robotics products. AI-driven revenues exceeded 60% of second-quarter sales as total revenues reached a second consecutive record of $1.33 billion and non-GAAP EPS rose to $2.47. Management now expects first-half revenue to represent 50% to 52% of the full year, versus the prior 55% to 60% view, reflecting better second-half visibility. Memory, auto and industrial, IST, Product Test and Robotics are expected to grow sequentially in the second half.
KEYS' Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates
Keysight has gained 102.6% in the past year compared with the Electronics - Measuring Instruments industry's growth of 91.3%.
Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 25.6 forward earnings, lower than 27.23 for the industry and lower than its mean of 30.45.
The company's earnings estimates for 2026 and 2027 have improved over the past 60 days.
KEYS sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

What Happened?
A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after weaker-than-expected U.S. employment data cooled Treasury yields, easing borrowing-cost pressure across the sector.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that nonfarm payrolls rose by 29,000 in September, falling far short of the 84,000 projected by economists polled by Dow Jones. The unemployment rate increased to 4.2%, while prior-month revisions removed 60,000 jobs, according to the agency. Treasury yields slumped following the release, as traders unwound expectations for another Federal Reserve rate increase, according to CNBC.
For industrials, falling yields reduce the cost of capital on large debt loads and ease financing for buyers of heavy machinery and commercial aircraft. However, the hiring slowdown introduces cyclical vulnerability. Slower payroll expansion signals potential cooling in manufacturing activity and construction, explaining why names tied to agricultural and aerospace end markets traded more cautiously.Cheaper capital helps equipment makers and suppliers by lowering the hurdle rate for customers financing multi-year orders. Yet because industrial revenue hinges on real economic throughput, the relief from lower rates will hold only if cooling labor conditions do not broaden into cancelled projects and deferred capital spending.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Keysight to Demonstrate Advanced Radio Frequency, 6G, and AI Solutions at European Microwave Week 2026
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 8:00 AM PDT 2 min read
SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 30, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies (NYSE: KEYS):
What: At European Microwave Week (EuMW) 2026, Keysight Technologies will showcase solutions that help engineers accelerate radio frequency (RF) and microwave innovation across industries including defense, space, broadband wireless, 5G and 6G. As a platinum sponsor, Keysight will also mark 25 years of support for EuMW.
Where: Keysight booth A20, ExCeL London, UK
More information: Keysight at European Microwave Week
Keysight demonstrations will include:
RF to sub-THz characterization: Explore Keysight's vector network analyzer (VNA) portfolio, to address the measurement challenges of next-generation high frequency designs. Measure active and passive components across research and development and production with scalable VNA solutions, including extended-frequency analysis for emerging high-frequency and sub-THz designs.
Signal Generation and Analysis: Evaluate true device performance with metrology-grade signal purity from the XG7-class signal generator, alongside high-performance wideband analysis of emerging V-band, satellite, and 6G waveforms with the XA6 signal analyzer.
Spectrum and PNT Resilience: Identify and locate interference, capture and replay in-phase and quadrature (IQ) data, and recreate realistic global navigation satellite system (GNSS) environments to validate positioning, navigation, and timing performance.
Next-Gen Connectivity: Keysight will show how to validate next-generation connectivity with realistic satellite link emulation, including orbital motion, Doppler, delay, beam dynamics, and fading, alongside ultra-wideband 6G waveform analysis and multi-channel MIMO evaluation.
AI-Driven Engineering: See how AI-enabled design and simulation workflows can help engineers evaluate design options, improve beamformer performance, and advance RF development.

Broadcom reports 86% revenue growth amid AI boom as Intel shows signs of recovery
Broadcom's AI chip sales more than tripled while Intel posted its own gains, but the two companies are running very different races
Broadcom just posted a quarter that makes most of the chip industry look like it’s standing still. Consolidated revenue for fiscal Q3 2026 hit $29.6 billion, up 86% from a year earlier.
Intel had good news too. Its Q2 2026 revenue climbed 25% to $16.1 billion.
The core of Broadcom’s quarter was AI semiconductors. That business brought in $16.7 billion, a 221% jump year over year.
AI chips made up 56% of total revenue, so more than half of every dollar the company booked came from AI hardware.
Profitability kept pace with the top line. Non-GAAP operating income reached $20.1 billion, up 92% year over year. Free cash flow came in at $13.7 billion, or 46% of revenue.
Management also signaled that the next quarter should be even bigger. Broadcom guided Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue to approximately $34.8 billion, which would represent 93% growth from the prior year.
The company raised its full-year fiscal 2026 AI revenue forecast to $58 billion. Its longer-range outlook calls for AI revenue of approximately $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and approximately $230 billion in fiscal 2028.
Broadcom’s confidence rests on supply agreements with some of the biggest names in AI. The customer list includes Google, Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

Anthropic is expected to become the largest customer for Broadcom’s custom AI accelerators, known as XPUs, by 2027.
An XPU is a chip designed for one customer’s specific AI workloads, rather than a general-purpose processor sold off the shelf. Custom silicon built around a customer’s own software tends to create long relationships, which helps explain why Broadcom feels comfortable publishing forecasts two fiscal years out.
Intel’s quarter told a recovery story rather than a boom story. Revenue of $16.1 billion was up 25% from the prior year.
The brightest spot was the Data Center and AI segment, or DCAI. That unit grew 59% to $6.3 billion.
Intel’s non-GAAP gross margin improved to approximately 41.8%, and losses in its foundry business narrowed.
CEO Lip-Bu Tan’s leadership appears to be having a positive effect on results. Still, Intel faces significant execution risk as it pushes its turnaround forward in a crowded, highly competitive market.
Two chipmakers, two different scoreboards
Broadcom’s AI semiconductor revenue alone, at $16.7 billion, edged past Intel’s entire quarterly revenue of $16.1 billion.
Broadcom’s AI segment grew 221%, while Intel’s DCAI unit grew 59%.
What this means for investors and the chip sector
Broadcom has turned AI demand into contracted, multi-year business with the industry’s largest buyers. Forecasts of approximately $230 billion in AI revenue by fiscal 2028 are still forecasts, not booked sales.
When more than half of revenue comes from AI chips sold to a relatively small group of hyperscalers and AI labs, any slowdown in their spending plans would show up quickly in the numbers. Anthropic’s expected rise to the top of the XPU customer list ties part of Broadcom’s future to how fast AI labs keep scaling their compute budgets.
Watch Broadcom’s Q4 results against its approximately $34.8 billion guidance, and watch whether Intel’s margin gains and foundry improvements hold over the next few quarters.

TL;DR: Intel's rumored Nova Lake-HX laptop CPUs may use Core Ultra 4000 names, while H-series and other mobile chips retain three-digit names such as Core Ultra 400. Intel hasn't confirmed the naming, and it may change before Nova Lake's expected early 2027 launch.

Intel's next laptop lineup might end up with two different naming schemes at once. According to leaker Jaykihn, "Nova Lake-HX" laptop chips will use the four-digit Core Ultra 4000 format that recently showed up in a leaked desktop lineup. H-series and suffix-less mobile chips, however, will apparently "continue the three-number naming of the prior generation."
So if this pans out, a gaming laptop with an HX chip would carry a Core Ultra 4000 name, while a thinner laptop from the same generation would sit under something like Core Ultra 400. That's the same generation and the same architecture, split by one extra digit. I think that's going to be fun to explain to anyone shopping for a laptop, since a bigger number usually reads as a newer or faster product. Jaykihn didn't share any HX model names, so we don't know what they will look like yet.
There is also some logic behind this new naming change. HX chips are usually based on desktop silicon, and Nova Lake-HX is said to top out at 28 cores, which matches the leaked desktop Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC. Leaker Golden Pig Upgrade reportedly put it more bluntly, saying Intel has too many SKUs for three digits.
Then there's the Haswell problem. Intel already sold a Core 4000 series back in 2013 and 2014, with chips like the Core i7-4770K and Core i7-4790K. The leaked Core Ultra 9 4950K and Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC come awfully close to old laptop parts like the Core i7-4950HQ and Core i7-4870HQ. The "Core Ultra" prefix technically keeps them apart, although I wouldn't bet on used listings and search results being that careful.

Intel Core Ultra 4000 naming extends beyond desktop
Intel’s four-digit Core Ultra naming for Nova Lake will reportedly apply to both desktop and HX laptop processors. Leaker Jaykihn has clarified that Nova Lake-HX processors will use the same four-number format recently seen in the leaked Nova Lake-S lineup.
This follows our earlier report on seven Nova Lake-S processors, including the Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC, Core Ultra 9 4950K and Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC. Those names already indicated that Intel was moving its desktop Series 4 processors from the three-digit format used by Core Ultra 200 to four-digit model numbers.
HX gets four digits, regular mobile stays with three
According to Jaykihn, laptop HX processors will also use four-digit model numbers. However, the change does not apply to the entire Nova Lake mobile lineup. H-series and suffix-less mobile processors will continue using the three-digit numbering introduced with previous Core Ultra generations.
This means Nova Lake could effectively use two numbering systems within the same generation. Desktop Nova Lake-S and laptop Nova Lake-HX would use names in the Core Ultra 4000 range, while mainstream mobile processors would remain within the three-digit Core Ultra 400 series.
Laptop HX chips also utilize this four-number naming, while H and suffix-less mobile continue the three-number naming of the prior generation. https://t.co/ZSucNCFGP8
Jaykihn also clarified another detail from the leaked desktop list. All of the Nova Lake processors reportedly include four LP-E cores and vPro support, even where those features were not listed in the original table. The seven leaked desktop models range from the Core Ultra 5 4650K/KF to the 28-core Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC.
Intel has not announced the Nova Lake model names yet. The leaked naming nevertheless now appears across multiple desktop SKUs and is reportedly also planned for HX processors, making the four-digit format broader than the Core Ultra 9 4950K engineering sample that first revealed the change.

Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) continues executing its AI-driven turnaround, backed by strong demand across CPUs, ASICs, advanced packaging, and its foundry network. Strategic moves include Nvidia partnership, SoftBank’s $2 billion investment, and progress on 18A process technology, reinforcing Intel’s push to reclaim semiconductor leadership.
Intel’s foundry story may have another catalyst investors are overlooking: a Terafab opportunity tied to Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI.
Pivot to Agentic AI and Processor Opportunity
For Intel, both advanced Agentic AI CPUs and the conventional computing have been the center of attention lately. The company is aiming to regain its competitive strength within the conventional server side. However, a strategic pivot toward agentic and inference deployments could augment the company’s core operations. Intel Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenue rose 59% year-over-year to $6.3 billion in the second quarter. The expansion exceeded the overall topline growth of 25% for the second quarter.
A double-edged sword for the company is the prevailing demand-supply dynamics. The company’s CEO, Lip-Bu Tan, recently highlighted that Intel can only meet roughly half of the processor demand. The capacity constraints could instill some skepticism, but there is another way to look at the situation. Such supply-related problem is something most companies would want to have, as it presents lucrative opportunity for players to expand their market share.
Narrowing down the supply-demand gap would require significant amount of substrate capacity expansion. The process is time consuming and requires large allocation of capital. The lag time could result in customer switching to alternatives.
The company’s 49% stake in chipmaker Altera, which has confidentially filed for a U.S. IPO, leads to an additional concern despite valuation prospects for Intel shareholders. The underlying AI capabilities will remain crucial during the market-making process, and there is a risk of such claims running ahead of operating realities. Investors will be keen on exploring roughly how much of the management’s mid-20% revenue expansion outlook for 2026, is tied to AI deployments.
The stock closed at $120.23 on September 30, translating into a 225.83% year-to-date return. A conventional trailing P/E is not meaningful because Intel remains loss-making on a trailing GAAP basis.
The forward P/E of 63.29x also appears highly inflated in isolation. But there might be further upside in the offering given the ongoing expectations of a sharp rise in earnings. However, that would demand a flawless execution from the management.

BlackRock is the largest institutional stakeholder, as per Yahoo Finance database, holding 426.48 million shares as of June 30. This amounts to 8.46% of outstanding shares. Other notable institutional investors include Vanguard Capital Management and State Street Corporation, holding 5.65% and 4.30% of outstanding shares respectively.
Future trajectory for Intel hinges on ensuring a successful transformation into a robust chip manufacturer. The company’s growing foundry business, advanced packaging and 18A process will remain integral to the broader strategy, while new offerings across data centers and PCs could also bolster its market standing.

Intel’s turnaround is starting to show up in its financial results. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC | INTC Price Prediction) posted Q2 revenue of $16.13B, up 25.4% year over year. CEO Lip-Bu Tan called it “our strongest revenue growth in more than fifteen years, enabled by greater speed, accountability, and customer focus.”
Intel 18A output came in approximately 25% above target, and management described Xeon 6 as “one of the fastest ramping products in Intel history.”
Shares are up 233.33% year to date to $123. The next question is how much further the stock can go. Here’s what Intel needs to do to hit $150 in 2027.
Wall Street Is Trailing Intel’s Rally, and Estimates Keep Rising
Analysts haven’t caught up with the stock. The consensus price target of $116.37 is about 5% below the current price. 32 analysts rate the stock Hold, compared with 13 Buy and 1 Strong Buy.
Earnings forecasts tell a more bullish story. Consensus 2027 EPS has rose to $2.0621 from $1.5245 90 days ago, an upward revision of roughly 35%. Analysts expect 2027 revenue of $72B, about 14% above the 2026 estimate, with EPS growing roughly 36%.
Can Intel Really Hit $150? Let’s Do the Math
At $123, Intel trades at about 60x consensus 2027 EPS. At $150, that multiple would rise to roughly 73x, far above the S&P 500’s forward multiple of about 21-23x.
The most bullish analyst expects $3.44 in 2027 EPS. At that level, $150 works out to about 44x. Intel keeps beating forecasts, making results near the high end realistic.
What Could Push Intel to $150?
Beat run: Q2 was Intel’s seventh consecutive quarter of exceeding expectations. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 beat the $0.2175 estimate.
Server CPU shortage: Server CPU demand “continues to far outpace available supply.” Data Center and AI revenue rose 59%, with operating profit at 40% of revenue.
Custom chips: This business approaches a $2 billion run rate with management expecting $4 billion soon against a market sized at over $100 billion.
Foundry progress: The foundry operating loss narrowed by $348 million from the prior quarter. Intel 14A risk production is on track for the second half of 2027.
Strategic partners: NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) made a $5B equity investment and picked Xeon 6 for its DGX Rubin NVL8 systems. SoftBank added $2B.
Hurdles remain. Intel Foundry lost $2.1 billion last quarter, and 2027 capital spending is expected to be “significantly above the 2026 levels.” With a beta of 2.231, the stock will swing more than the broader market.
Intel’s History Says a 22% Move Is Well Within Range
Reaching $150 requires a gain of about 22%, small next to this year’s 233.33% run. In 2023, shares rose roughly 90% before giving that gain back. Intel also traded as high as $142.35 within the past 52 weeks, not far below the target.
Hitting $150 requires a roughly 22% gain. EPS estimates are rising quickly, Intel keeps beating them, and server demand is ahead of supply. If 18A keeps ramping and custom chip and foundry businesses scale, earnings could rose enough to support a higher price.
That’s the plan for outsized returns in 2027, and the same set of early signs we cataloged in a free playbook on spotting the next Nvidia before the headlines catch on.

Intel shares fall nearly 9% in two sessions as investors reassess valuation.
Server CPU demand stays strong even as traditional PC demand remains soft.
TD Cowen sees limited upside while Melius argues Intel could still top $200.
Intel stock NASDAQ:INTC is testing the conviction behind Wall Street’s biggest semiconductor comeback trades after erasing nearly 10% across two trading sessions.
The stock closed Monday around $116.03 after falling 5.67%, following a 3.5% decline on Friday.
The retreat came as higher Treasury yields, expensive oil and renewed pressure on technology shares triggered profit-taking after Intel’s 2026 run.
Yet the operating factors has not collapsed. Server processors remain in heavy demand, pricing power has improved and some analysts still see upside from Intel’s foundry ambitions.
Intel’s turnaround is intact but the easy money may not be
There was no fresh earnings warning behind Monday’s selloff.
Intel’s latest quarter showed revenue of $16.1 billion, up 25% from a year earlier, while adjusted earnings of $0.42 a share beat expectations.
Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan has also said AI is driving unprecedented demand for compute, with server CPU demand running ahead of supply.
The macro backdrop instead became less forgiving. The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.2% as oil remained above $105 a barrel, putting pressure on richly valued technology stocks.
Higher yields matter particularly for shares that have undergone dramatic re-ratings because investors discount future earnings more heavily.
That distinction is important. Intel is not falling because its comeback has failed, but investors have dramatically raised the price they were willing to pay for that comeback.
The stock had risen more than 200% this year before the latest pullback, making valuation difficult to ignore.
Wall Street now wants proof Intel can grow into the price
TD Cowen captured that concern days before the selloff.
The brokerage reiterated a Hold rating and $115 price target on September 24. Its analysts said “things are moving in the right direction” but argued investors need visibility towards more than $100 billion of Products revenue and over $20 billion of Foundry revenue. Intel generated roughly $57 billion of trailing revenue at the time.
That target now sits almost exactly where the shares trade.
Market data shows the average Wall Street target around $116, highlighting how far the stock’s rally had already moved towards consensus expectations.
The implication is that sentiment alone may no longer be enough. Intel may now need materially better revenue, margins and foundry execution to restart the rally.
That does not make the turnaround thesis wrong, but it raises the hurdle for every new catalyst.
The bull case still sees two valuable Intels
Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes remains considerably more optimistic.
Reitzes maintained a Buy rating and $165 target this month and noted that Intel could ultimately exceed $200 within two years.
His thesis effectively separates Intel into two businesses, with the Products franchise and foundry operation potentially commanding substantial standalone value.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Srini Pajjuri offers a useful complication.
He recently described PC and smartphone demand as “weak but stable”, with desktop demand particularly soft, while estimating Intel’s x86 server CPU volumes could rise around 15% to 20% as supply catches up with AI-related demand.
That makes Intel increasingly a two-speed company. Traditional PC demand remains uninspiring, while AI infrastructure is supporting unusually strong server demand and pricing.
The next phase of the rally will therefore be harder than the first, as improving sentiment helped investors revalue Intel dramatically.

iMac (Retina 4K, 21.5-inch, 2019) now vintage worldwide
Apple maintains a list of vintage and obsolete products, which lets users know whether older devices are still eligible for hardware service and replacement parts.
The company considers a product vintage once it has been off the market for more than five but less than seven years. Products may become obsolete once Apple has stopped distributing them for more than seven years.
Apple doesn’t necessarily move products to the obsolete list as soon as they cross that threshold, as service and parts availability can vary by product. That said, once a product is classified as obsolete, Apple and its authorized service providers generally stop offering hardware service for it, and parts can no longer be ordered.
Today, the company added the iMac (Retina 4K, 21.5-inch, 2019) to its vintage products list, which means it may still be eligible for hardware service and replacement parts, but they’re subject to availability.
In practice, if you own this iMac and have been putting off a repair, it might be a good idea to get it serviced sooner rather than later.

Intel's (INTC -0.56%) comeback has been quite a sight to behold. As of this writing, shares of the chipmaker have exploded by more than 220% in 2026 in part due to surging demand for the company's CPUs, but also due to increased optimism about the outlook for its foundry business. And even with that incredible run-up behind it, patient investors may still want to consider buying Intel's stock.

Intel's second quarter was one of its best in several years. Revenue jumped by 25% year over year to more than $16 billion. Intel's gross margin also improved tremendously, rising to 40.4% from 27.5%.
The bigger story here is Intel's foundry division and the turnaround happening within it. Intel Foundry's revenue was nearly $6 billion in the quarter, and its output paced 25% above the target. While the segment posted a $2.1 billion loss, the gap is narrowing. Foundry revenue from external customers was just $293 million, which means that if its turnaround is to gain steam, Intel really needs to win more business from outside clients.
The company's GAAP loss was $2.16 per share, but it's important to note that this was largely due to an escrow arrangement related to funds it was awarded through the CHIPS Act. On the books, that showed up in the form of a non-cash charge of $12.53 billion. So the quarter's loss was not reflective of operational issues.
Image source: The Motley Fool.
Much of Intel Foundry's future success hangs on the successful launch of Intel 14A. This is a next-generation semiconductor fabrication process node that will produce chips with even greater transistor density than 2-nanometer chips. The development of its 14A foundry is nearing completion, with risk production planned for 2027 and a high-volume mass-production target of 2028. Management's hope is that its 14A manufacturing services will position it to pose a serious challenge to Taiwan Semiconductor's dominance in cutting-edge chip manufacturing.

In a bullish sign, Intel CFO David Zinsner implied on the Q2 earnings call that the development is going very well and that conversations with potential customers have shifted from evaluating 14A to inquiring about how much capacity they can secure.
It's been reported that a slew of megacaps, including most of the "Magnificent Seven," are among Intel's prospective foundry clients. However, Intel will need to secure one of these large-scale customers sooner rather than later.
In June, Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya gave Intel stock an unusual double-upgrade from underperform to buy, citing an optimistic outlook for its foundry business and strong demand. Intel did have to engage in a $23 billion secondary stock sale in August to help fund its foundry build-out.
Intel is due to report its third-quarter earnings on Oct. 22. The company's guidance suggests revenue could be as high as $16.8 billion. One concern is that Intel's valuation is sky-high right now. The company for years maintained a forward P/E ratio in the low teens. Now that metric stands at more than 60.
Furthermore, the consensus price target among analysts is just above $116 per share, and the stock is trading above that as of this writing. There isn't much room for error with Intel's stock.
However, given the company's main revenue sources and an ever-improving foundry operation, I'm quite bullish on Intel's future -- as long as its 14A process node proves as promising as advertised. For interested investors, it may be prudent to build a position in Intel slowly rather than all at once, given the milestones the company still needs to hit over the next couple of years.

Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) continues executing its AI-driven turnaround, backed by strong demand across CPUs, ASICs, advanced packaging, and its foundry network. Strategic moves include Nvidia partnership, SoftBank's $2 billion investment, and progress on 18A process technology, reinforcing Intel's push to reclaim semiconductor leadership.
Intel's foundry story may have another catalyst investors are overlooking: a Terafab opportunity tied to Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI.
Is Intel's Data Center Comeback Real, or Just a Supply Squeeze in Disguise?
Pivot to Agentic AI and Processor Opportunity
For Intel, both advanced Agentic AI CPUs and the conventional computing have been the center of attention lately. The company is aiming to regain its competitive strength within the conventional server side. However, a strategic pivot toward agentic and inference deployments could augment the company's core operations. Intel Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenue rose 59% year-over-year to $6.3 billion in the second quarter. The expansion exceeded the overall topline growth of 25% for the second quarter.
A double-edged sword for the company is the prevailing demand-supply dynamics. The company's CEO, Lip-Bu Tan, recently highlighted that Intel can only meet roughly half of the processor demand. The capacity constraints could instill some skepticism, but there is another way to look at the situation. Such supply-related problem is something most companies would want to have, as it presents lucrative opportunity for players to expand their market share.
Narrowing down the supply-demand gap would require significant amount of substrate capacity expansion. The process is time consuming and requires large allocation of capital. The lag time could result in customer switching to alternatives.
The company's 49% stake in chipmaker Altera, which has confidentially filed for a U.S. IPO, leads to an additional concern despite valuation prospects for Intel shareholders. The underlying AI capabilities will remain crucial during the market-making process, and there is a risk of such claims running ahead of operating realities. Investors will be keen on exploring roughly how much of the management's mid-20% revenue expansion outlook for 2026, is tied to AI deployments.
The stock closed at $120.23 on September 30, translating into a 225.83% year-to-date return. The rally has pushed the company's market capitalization to $635.55 billion, which is roughly 11 times its trailing revenue of $57.03 billion. A conventional trailing P/E is not meaningful because Intel remains loss-making on a trailing GAAP basis.
The forward P/E of 63.29x also appears highly inflated in isolation. But there might be further upside in the offering given the ongoing expectations of a sharp rise in earnings. However, that would demand a flawless execution from the management.

BlackRock is the largest institutional stakeholder, as per Yahoo Finance database, holding 426.48 million shares as of June 30. This amounts to 8.46% of outstanding shares. Other notable institutional investors include Vanguard Capital Management and State Street Corporation, holding 5.65% and 4.30% of outstanding shares respectively.

The company's growing foundry business, advanced packaging and 18A process will remain integral to the broader strategy, while new offerings across data centers and PCs could also bolster its market standing.

The proximate catalyst was Meta’s Muse AI agent, which triggered a broad CPU rally, but the more interesting point is sequencing. Tigress Financial’s $145 target on Intel landed before this move, not after it. The target led, and the price is now chasing the thesis rather than the other way around.
The bull case rests on a foundry-execution bet: Intel 18A yields, 14A customer commitments, and Terafab progress at a valuation that leaves no slack for a slipped tape-out.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) rose 24.75% over the same five sessions, and NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) added 7.78%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) rose 6.77%. Intel outran the pack, but the sector context is unmistakable.
Strip out the AI CPU rotation and the company-specific delta is smaller than the headline suggests.
Consensus tells a different story. Alpha Vantage lists an average analyst target of $116.37 against a 52-week high of $142.35. The ratings split is 1 strong buy, 13 buy, 32 hold, 1 sell, 1 strong sell. The $145 print is one shop’s view, not a herd.

The $5 billion NVIDIA equity investment and Xeon 6’s selection for NVIDIA’s DGX Rubin NVL8 systems are real anchors. Ohio memory production talks remain unconfirmed.

The bear case is that foundry losses persist, PC consumption falls into the low double digits in 2026, and $20 billion-plus capex requires capital markets. A slip on 14A PDK 0.9 in October would compress the multiple fast.
The deciding variable is external foundry revenue conversion. Until $293 million becomes a multi-billion run rate with named customers, this remains a narrative trade priced as a fundamental one.
